{
  "overview": "This chapter details the architecture and operational mechanics of an AI tutor system, beginning with language model training protocols that emphasize dataset separation to prevent overstatement of performance. It explores the internal workings of decoder-only transformers, including tokenization, causal attention masks, and the distinction between attention weights and factual truth. The text further covers optimization techniques such as loss functions, backpropagation, and regularization methods like dropout and early stopping to mitigate overfitting. Post-training strategies are examined, specifically weight quantization for efficiency and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for dynamic knowledge access without retraining. Finally, the chapter establishes a dual-evaluation framework that separates retrieval quality from answer generation, requiring tutors to explicitly identify conflicts in course passages rather than synthesizing unsupported conclusions.",

    "AI tutor functionality and limitations regarding factual accuracy",
    "Language model training mechanisms including parameter adjustment",
    "Roles of training, validation, and held-out test datasets",
    "Importance of dataset separation to avoid data leakage",
    "Distinction between dataset size and dataset quality",
    "Decoder-only transformer architecture",

    "Positional information in sequences",

    "Learning rate impact: balancing stability against improvement speed",
    "Overfitting definition: training performance not translating to unseen examples",

    "Early stopping strategy: using validation performance to determine training end",
    "Weight quantization for memory reduction",
    "Impact of precision reduction on answer quality",
    "Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mechanism",
    "Embedding mapping and similarity search",
    "Updating document indices without retraining",
    "Limitations of retrieved passages (irrelevance, outdated content)",
    "Distinction between retrieval recall and precision",
    "Evaluation of factual correctness versus retrieval metrics",
